+---
+author: Mari Schneider (nschneid95@gmail.com)
+state: draft

+
+# RFD Job Service
+
+## Required Approvers
+
+- rosstimothy || nklaassen || GavinFrazar
+
+## What
+
+A job service that will be able to run arbitrary linux jobs in a managed container environment. Users will be able to easily manage any number of jobs and easily access the outputs of all of them. Reasonable resource controls will be applied to each job.
+
+## Why
+
+As requested by Teleport for us to get a feel around each other.
+
+## Details
+
+### Server
+
+#### API
+
+ - *StartJob*: Tells the server to start a new job executing the given command with the given arguments. The server responds with the ID of the started job.
+ - *StopJob*: Tells the server to kill a currently running job specified by an ID number. If the job is already stopped this does nothing.
+ - *GetStatus*: Requests the current status of the job specified by an ID number. In addition to running/done/failed status the server will include any error code returned by the process.
+ - *GetOutput*: Requests any output from the job, either STDOUT or STDERR
+
+#### Implementation
+
+Every job will be stored in a global map from ID to job info. This will contain the Process object as well as capture and store both outputs from the task. While this limits the concurrency of the server, most RPCs are quick calls. The only long lasting RPC is GetOutput, and we can hang onto the job info object directly for this RPC (so we don't need to hold onto a lock for the map for long).
comment.body: Yeah, I meant global variable as in every thread can access it. I figured a map would be well suited to the "lookup by ID" style that most of the RPCs are formatted in.

comment.body:
Logically it is required. However, there are three separate ways to make this field required:
1. Use proto2 and mark it as `required`. While this enforces the field being set on the client side, it is not very portable in the future and, therefore, I prefer to avoid it.
2. Use proto3 and do not mark it. This does not force the client to set the field, and the server cannot tell if the field is set explicitly or via default value. While we could probably assume a user wouldn't set an empty string, this can be more complicated in other cases (such as the ID fields). Therefore I tend to avoid this approach as well.
3. Use proto2/proto3 and mark it as `optional`. While the client is still able to omit the field, the server can (and will) check if the field was explicitly set and reject the request if it is not. Although it can be slightly confusing in the proto file and results in a server side error response rather than a client side error (wasted time/resources), I still have found this to be the best approach.

@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+---
+author: Mari Schneider (nschneid95@gmail.com)
+state: draft
+---
+
+# RFD Job Service
+
+## Required Approvers
+
+- rosstimothy || nklaassen || GavinFrazar
+
+## What
+
+A job service that will be able to run arbitrary linux jobs in a managed container environment. Users will be able to easily manage any number of jobs and easily access the outputs of all of them. Reasonable resource controls will be applied to each job.
+
+## Why
+
+As requested by Teleport for us to get a feel around each other.
+
+## Details
+
+### Server
+
+#### API
+
+ - *StartJob*: Tells the server to start a new job executing the given command with the given arguments. The server responds with the ID of the started job.
+ - *StopJob*: Tells the server to kill a currently running job specified by an ID number. If the job is already stopped this does nothing.
+ - *GetStatus*: Requests the current status of the job specified by an ID number. In addition to running/done/failed status the server will include any error code returned by the process.
+ - *GetOutput*: Requests any output from the job, either STDOUT or STDERR
+
+#### Implementation
+
+The first thing the server will do is check for/create the job_service cgroups. This will use cgroups v1 (since that is what my system is currently using). It will create a job_service group under the cpu, memory, and blkio controllers. The cpu shares will be set to 1, the memory high limit will be set to 1G, and the blkio read/write limit will be set to 1 MB/s. If the group already exists, the procs file will be cleared.
+
+Every job will be stored in a global map from ID to job info. This will contain the Process object as well as capture and store both outputs from the task. While this limits the concurrency of the server, most RPCs are quick calls. The only long lasting RPC is GetOutput, and we can hang onto the job info object directly for this RPC (so we don't need to hold onto a lock for the map for long).
+
+There will also be a global nextID field that gets incremented every time a new job is started. The will be protected by the same locks as the map.
+
+Jobs will be run using the [exec](https://pkg.go.dev/os/exec) package. Output will be forwarded to any listening RPC handlers as well as stored in a [string.Builder](https://pkg.go.dev/strings#Builder.String) to be forwarded to any future RPC callers. The first thing a started job will do is enlist itself in the job_service cgroups. Then it will run the user command. When a user kills a job, the server will call [Kill](https://pkg.go.dev/os#Process.Kill) on the process and update the job map to indicate that the job was killed. Any streaming RPCs for this job will be finished and closed.
comment.body: I'm going to set the cgroup in the Cmd's parameters to ensure that the job starts in the appropriate cgroup.

+The first thing the server will do is check for/create the job_service cgroups. This will use cgroups v1 (since that is what my system is currently using). It will create a job_service group under the cpu, memory, and blkio controllers. The cpu shares will be set to 1, the memory high limit will be set to 1G, and the blkio read/write limit will be set to 1 MB/s. If the group already exists, the procs file will be cleared.
+
+Every job will be stored in a global map from ID to job info. This will contain the Process object as well as capture and store both outputs from the task. While this limits the concurrency of the server, most RPCs are quick calls. The only long lasting RPC is GetOutput, and we can hang onto the job info object directly for this RPC (so we don't need to hold onto a lock for the map for long).
+
+There will also be a global nextID field that gets incremented every time a new job is started. The will be protected by the same locks as the map.
+
+Jobs will be run using the [exec](https://pkg.go.dev/os/exec) package. Output will be forwarded to any listening RPC handlers as well as stored in a [string.Builder](https://pkg.go.dev/strings#Builder.String) to be forwarded to any future RPC callers. The first thing a started job will do is enlist itself in the job_service cgroups. Then it will run the user command. When a user kills a job, the server will call [Kill](https://pkg.go.dev/os#Process.Kill) on the process and update the job map to indicate that the job was killed. Any streaming RPCs for this job will be finished and closed.
+
+#### Security
+
+The server will be run as a designated user and store its certificate in ~/job_service/cert.pem and its private key in ~/job_service/key.key. Connections will be made with the [http](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http) and [tls](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls) go libraries. I will be using TLS 1.3 because it is both the generally reccomended version as well as considered more secure. Unfortunately, this means I am unable to specify a cipher suite in Go (it will always use a default list), but this isn't a secuirity risk and there are no special restrictions to take into account here. Although authorizing clients per RPC endpoint would be nice (for example, allowing some users to get outputs without the ability to start/stop jobs), for this project I'm going to restrict it to a single authorized/not authorized per user. +- rosstimothy || nklaassen || GavinFrazar
+
+## What
+
+A job service that will be able to run arbitrary linux jobs in a managed container environment. Users will be able to easily manage any number of jobs and easily access the outputs of all of them. Reasonable resource controls will be applied to each job.
+
+## Why
+
+As requested by Teleport for us to get a feel around each other.
+
+## Details
+
+### Server
+
+#### API
+
+ - *StartJob*: Tells the server to start a new job executing the given command with the given arguments. The server responds with the ID of the started job.
+ - *StopJob*: Tells the server to kill a currently running job specified by an ID number. If the job is already stopped this does nothing.
+ - *GetStatus*: Requests the current status of the job specified by an ID number. In addition to running/done/failed status the server will include any error code returned by the process.
+ - *GetOutput*: Requests any output from the job, either STDOUT or STDERR
+
+#### Implementation
+
+The first thing the server will do is check for/create the job_service cgroups.
+This will use cgroups v2.
+It will create a job_service group under the cpu, memory, and io controllers.
+This will be a container to hold all job specific cgroups.
+The server will also read the /proc/partitions file to find the major/minor device numbers of all hard drives.
+This will be used later when setting io limits.
+
+Information about a job will be stored in a `Job` object:
+````go
+type Job struct {
+	// Holds information about and access to the underlying process running this job
+	cmd           exec.Cmd
+	// Sets of stream handles that are listening to the output of this job
+	stdOutStreams map[GetOutputStream]struct{}
+	stdErrStreams map[GetOutputStream]struct{}
+	// Buffers storing job output for future GetOutput calls
+	stdOutBuffer  bytes.Buffer
+	stdErrBuffer  bytes.Buffer
+	// Records if this job was killed by a StopJob RPC.
+	killedByUser  bool
+	// Owning user
+	user          string
+	// Job ID
+	id            int
+}
+````
+
+The server will have a global map from ID to `Job`.
+
+When a new job is started, the server will create a new cgroup dedicated to it and set reasonable values: 1 cpu share, 1G memory, and 1 MB/s disk.
+A new UUID will be generated for the job.
+The job will then be started and inserted into the map before the id is returned to the client.
+When StopJob is called, every job in the dedicated cgroup will be killed and the cgroup will be removed.
+Any open GetOutput streams will be flushed and closed.
+The job will still stay in the map so future GetStatus calls can be properly handled.
+A GetOutput call will first send back any output stored in the buffer, chucking if needed.
+If the job is still running the stream will be added to the job's stream set to receive any future output.
+
+### Client
+
+#### CLI
+
+The client CLI will be a light wrapper around the API. The first argument specifies which command to run (i.e. which RPC to send) and any following arguments fill the RPC fields). For example:
+
+````code
+$ job_service start ls -a
+$ job_service stop $ID
+$ job_service status $ID
+$ job_service output $ID STDOUT
+````
+
+The output request will continue streaming output to STDOUT until the server closes the connection (due to shutting down or the end of the output stream).
+
+### Authorization
+
+There will be a server certificate that identifies the server as itself.
+Every client will expect this certificate from the server.
+There will also be a client side certificate that authenticates all users.
+The server will expect a user certificate signed by this client side certificate for every RPC call.
